title: Spin the playlist
scenario: Spin this playlist 2 places to the right — the end wraps around to the front.

intro.job: Spin this playlist 2 places to the right — the end wraps around to the front.

idea.rule: Rotating right takes from the end — a negative slice grabs the tail.
idea.detail: Spinning right by k means the last k songs wrap around to the front, and everything else moves along behind them. nums[-k:] is the tail — the last k songs — and nums[:-k] is everything before it. Tail first, then the rest. Slicing from the front (nums[k:]) moves things LEFT instead.

watch.code:
nums, k = pair
answer = nums[-k:] + nums[:-k]
print(answer)

model_restatement: Move every song k places to the right, with the last k wrapping around to the front.

clarify.question: Right or left?
clarify.answer: Right — the end wraps around to the front.

clarify.question: Could k be bigger than the playlist?
In place, or a new list?
clarify.answer: A new list is fine today.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Cut the playlist at k: the part after the cut goes first, then the part before it. Print it.
draft_code:
nums, k = pair
answer = nums[k:] + nums[:k]
print(answer)

checkpoints.prompt: On the print line, what is answer?
With the fix — on the print line, what is answer?

why_line: nums[k:] + nums[:k] puts everything from position 2 on first and moves the front two to the end — that's a LEFT spin. Spinning right takes the last two to the front.

explain.rule: Cutting from the front is turning the dial the wrong way — the front songs slide off the end instead of the end songs wrapping round to the front.
explain.bridge: Spinning right, which two songs should end up at the front?

fix.rule: nums[-k:] + nums[:-k]: the last k songs first, then everything before them.

walk.gloss: The playlist and how far to spin.
The tail (last k) goes first, then the rest.

fix.recommended:
nums, k = pair
answer = nums[-k:] + nums[:-k]
print(answer)

alternatives.code:
nums, k = pair
for _ in range(k):
    nums.insert(0, nums.pop())
print(nums)
alternatives.note: Move the last song to the front, k times — correct, and it shows what the slice is doing.

hints: Which songs are at the front of answer — the end of the playlist, or the middle?
Slicing from the front moves things left. Right takes from the end.
